questions.q: Which of these is one of Lambda's hard ceilings that makes it unsuitable for large-scale ETL?
options: A 15-minute maximum execution time
A maximum of 5 total invocations per day
No ability to read from S3
A requirement to use only Python
questions.explain: Lambda's 15-minute timeout is a hard ceiling that a large, long-running transformation job simply cannot fit inside.

questions.q: What is the maximum memory a single Lambda function can be configured with?
options: There is no maximum
questions.explain: Lambda memory tops out at 10,240 MB, which can be too little for large in-memory joins or aggregations on production-scale data.

questions.q: What is the deeper reason Lambda struggles with large-scale ETL, beyond the timeout and memory numbers themselves?
options: A single Lambda invocation runs on one instance, with no built-in distributed processing across a cluster
Lambda cannot be triggered by S3 events
Lambda functions cannot write to S3
Lambda requires manual server provisioning
questions.explain: Unlike Glue or EMR, which spread work across many workers in parallel, one Lambda invocation is a single instance with no built-in distributed engine.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's a common real-world pattern combining Lambda with large-scale ETL tools?
options: Lambda acts as a lightweight trigger that kicks off a Glue job, rather than doing the heavy processing itself
Lambda always replaces Glue and EMR entirely once a pipeline matures
Glue jobs trigger Lambda functions to do all the heavy processing
Lambda and Glue can never be used in the same pipeline
questions.explain: A frequent pattern is Lambda reacting to an event (like a file landing) and starting a Glue job, letting each tool do the part it's actually built for.

questions.q: What is Lambda's ephemeral /tmp storage limit per invocation?
options: Up to 10,240 MB
Unlimited
1 MB
It doesn't exist — Lambda has no local disk at all
questions.explain: Lambda provides up to 10,240 MB of temporary local disk in /tmp per invocation — enough for moderate intermediate files, not for large datasets that need to spill to disk.
